limitations: Text only; native audio and vision have not been tested.
Small hand-labelled paired-paraphrase set; not a production accuracy estimate.
Offset 0 is the last prompt token, predicting the first output token. No native output tokens generated.
Earlier offsets are causal next-token logits, not trained classification heads.
Future-token controls preserve batch shape; truncated prefixes separately test deployment behaviour.
Early-exit gate is selected on development examples only; the small held-out set cannot establish safety.
Thresholds apply to probabilities conditioned on labels; vocabulary mass is reported separately.
Five server parity checks generate one output token; the native probe only evaluates prompts.
Probe times include multiple logits and statistics, without prefix caching, alongside the live server.
interpretation: The strongest early position is offset -3, the newline immediately after the user-turn closing token.
Earlier positions do not contain consistently usable routing answers; a high conditional label probability can coincide with tiny total vocabulary mass on labels.
The development-selected early gate exits on 34/62 held-out variants with 2 errors; fallback to the final position gives 58/62 correct, versus 59/62 at the final position alone.
Offset 0 already provides a classification without sampling or generating a token. The native final scores agree with all five HTTP parity choices.
The early gate saves three prompt/header tokens, not an entire autoregressive transformer pass. This experiment does not measure a deployment speedup.

reproduction.notes: Uses live catalog and template endpoints. Exact historical prompts, option mappings, model statistics and prefix results are retained in the compressed details artifact.
